claims.statement: The #456 mutation layer exists because coverage cannot distinguish a test that fails when code breaks from a test that merely executes a changed line — diff-cover at --fail-under 100 proves only execution — so mutmut mutates the changed functions, and a killed-mutant score computed only from tests that run without a container is what exposes a fully-covered change as still untested.

Mutation scope is derived rather than typed: gauntlet-456.sh lists changed Python sources with `git diff --name-only <GAUNTLET_BASE>...HEAD -- 'src/harnessed/*.py'` (logged to mutation-scope.txt) so glue changed alongside the logic is mutated too, with the base overridable via GAUNTLET_BASE so the script keeps working across rebases and renames.

tools/mutation-targets-456.txt is the single source of the changed-function list for both mutation layers — gauntlet-456.sh appends `*` to each line as mutmut run filters and mutation-verdict-456.sh loops the same lines to demand killed mutants and no survivors — because when it was two hand-edited lists they had already drifted: eight changed decision functions (the docker --user/ownership/netns half of #456) appeared in neither, raised on PR #461 review.

mutmut names mutants `harnessed.<module>.x_<function>__mutmut_N` (no `src.` prefix, `x_` before the function, `x__` when the function is private), the targets list uses exactly this spelling for the sixteen #456-changed functions, and both scripts hard-fail if the targets file parses to nothing so an emptied list fails the layer rather than silently skipping it.

A mutmut filter matching nothing is silent — mutmut exits 0, generates the mutants tree, and `mutmut results` reports every mutant `not checked`, indistinguishable from a clean run — which is why the gauntlet runs `mutmut results` unconditionally and reads its output rather than its exit code; on the layer's first pass the gauntlet reported all-layers-passed over 51 survivors and five filters that had matched nothing at all.

mutmut generates zero mutants for an lru_cache-decorated function, so paths._detect_runtime and paths._probe_docker_rootless are deliberately plain functions beside the lru_cache(maxsize=1) wrappers active_runtime and docker_is_rootless — the combined versions produced no mutants and a clean report while the layer was blind to every refuse-rather-than-guess branch, and hoisting the bodies back into the caches reintroduces that blindness.

mutmut's tree copy dereferences symlinks, so catalog/*.local arrive as real directories and link-asserting tests (test_dynstack.py::test_the_default_recipe_ships_the_authoring_skill) fail inside the mutants tree, making the runner report `failed to collect stats` and execute no mutants; mutmut 3 exposes no --tests-dir flag, so gauntlet-456.sh narrows `tests_dir` in pyproject.toml via a scripted edit guarded by an assert of exactly one `tests_dir = ["tests/"]` occurrence, with a trap restoring the original file on EXIT/INT/TERM.

Every mutmut invocation in the gauntlet exports HARNESSED_DIR=$PWD because paths.harnessed_home() resolves harnessed's home through the src/harnessed/catalog symlink, which does not exist in the mutants tree.

The mutants/ tree is deleted before every mutmut run because mutmut caches its test-to-function mapping there and does not re-collect stats for tests created after the tree was built, so a stale tree reports newly-covered functions as `🫥 no tests` — measured: 30 mutants across _detect_runtime and _probe_docker_rootless sat at no-tests through two full runs with passing tests calling them directly; a cache that reports "nothing tests this" when something does is a fail-open in the layer that exists to catch fail-opens.

[tool.mutmut] shapes the score's honesty: paths_to_mutate is src/harnessed/, and also_copy copies whole directories (tests/, .github/, catalog/, tools/, schemas/, mise.toml, README.md) because the suite asserts repo assets and imports support/conftest as top-level modules — anything a test reads must exist in the mutants tree or every mutant reports "survived" for want of a runnable suite — and a mutant must be killed by a test running without a container, or the score measures the HARNESSED_PODMAN gate rather than the tests.

The mutation layer is judged by tools/mutation-verdict-456.sh, not by mutmut's exit code (which is 0 whether every mutant died or every one survived); reading mutation-targets-456.txt so it certifies exactly the functions the run mutated, it counts per function from the run log the statuses 🎉 killed, 🙁 survived, 🫥 no-tests, and fails the layer when killed+survived+no-tests is zero (silent filter), when no-tests is nonzero (uncovered, not passing — counted separately so the verdict says which of the two happened), or when any survivor is not an exact line in the classified allowlist.

The verdict checks the allowlist in reverse — every entry must still match a surviving mutant in the log — and distinguishes two kinds of stale with different remedies: a mutant that still exists but is now killed means a test got stronger (delete the entry), while a mutant that no longer exists means the source state changed and every other numbered entry for that function is suspect and must be re-read; found on the PR #461 review pass where 13 _preflight_runtime entries named numbers the function no longer generates.

The verdict's survivor grep uses the braced pattern "${fn}__mutmut_" deliberately: unbraced $fn__mutmut_ parses as the unset variable fn__mutmut_, the pattern matches nothing, and every survivor would pass unclassified — shellcheck SC1087 caught it, the same silently-matching-nothing failure shape this layer exists to catch.

mutation-verdict-456.sh is split out of gauntlet-456.sh and takes the log path as an argument so it can be run and controlled on its own against a known-bad input — inline, the only way to exercise it was a 15-minute full gauntlet, which meant in practice it was never exercised at all, and a gate nobody can cheaply run is a gate nobody has proven can fail.

Every entry in tools/mutation-allowlist-456.txt is one classified claim ("this mutant survives and no behaviour turns on it"), and the single class ever listed is mutmut's string mutation of error-message text ("x" -> "XXxXX", case inversion), allowed only because no branch, comparison, or call argument reads a message literal; mutants that changed exit codes or command argv were fixed with tests, never listed, so the file contains only ctrquery.x__runtime, capability.x__runtime, launcher.x__preflight_runtime and persist.x_guard_ownership message entries.

The classification stays narrow because the tests assert real message content: guard_ownership's message must name the path, the cause ("rootless"), the uid, "subuid", BOTH remediations, "docker info" in the unreadable-daemon variant, and the bare pinned mapping; _preflight_runtime's must name cause/uid/subuid/both remediations and exit 1; _runtime's must name the missing runtimes and exit 1 — each per-function reason names the assertions that keep it from being a blanket pass.

tools/regen-allowlist-456.py only records what survived a run log into the allowlist and never classifies: it refuses to write an empty allowlist, and it refuses any function whose survivors lack a REASONS entry (a new function with survivors is a classification decision, not a regeneration), so its output can only ever carry message-text-only reasons and a survivor of any other shape surfaces as an unclassifiable refusal rather than a widened allowlist.

Regeneration is not a fix — rerunning regen-allowlist-456.py over a fresh log lists every survivor and therefore passes, the gaming move the gate exists to prevent — so removals are explained in the allowlist header, which records PR #461's two distinct removal reasons (_preflight_runtime__mutmut_12 still exists but is now killed; _preflight_runtime__mutmut_23.._35 no longer exist because the function now generates 21 mutants).

tools/show-survivors-456.py prints each surviving mutant as a unified diff against its x_<fn>__mutmut_orig sibling by parsing mutants/src/harnessed/<module>.py with ast — read-only, avoiding mutmut show's ~40-second per-survivor package rebuild — and reports any survivor it cannot locate (missing mutants file or missing function pair) with a count and exit 1 ("classification is INCOMPLETE") instead of skipping it, because a classifier that quietly drops what it cannot parse produces a short list that looks like progress; the reporting replaced a FileNotFoundError crash on PR #461 review.

gauntlet-456.sh runs every layer even after one fails and exits nonzero at the end if any failed — fail-fast was measured wrong three times because a red diff-cover meant the two randomized-order runs and the entire mutation layer never executed, so the report could say nothing about them — with each layer's full output captured under GAUNTLET_LOGS and its exit code printed, under set -euo pipefail with no swallowed exit codes.

The property tests that kill survivors' neighbours are themselves shaped by the mutation layer: hypothesis properties over _without_userns (removes every --userns spelling and nothing else, identity when none present, idempotence) and pod_host_uid (only a keep-id mapping onto the image uid resolves; bare keep-id, auto, nomap and every other mode answers None) are module-level functions because under mutmut the same file executes from repo-tree and mutants-tree executors and hypothesis fails HealthCheck.differing_executors on a test method across two self executors sharing one example database, with monkeypatch used as a context manager so patches cannot leak between generated examples.

The assertions that kill survivors' neighbours pin content, not execution: test_docker_userns asserts typer.Exit exit_code == 1 (Exit(None)/Exit(0) also raise and both mean success; two surviving mutants sat exactly there) plus cause/uid/subuid/both remediations (15 message mutants survived while only one substring was asserted), and test_persist_allowlist asserts "--userns=" not in msg so the removeprefix-to-removesuffix mutant dies even though the positive substring assertion holds either way.

paths._probe_docker_rootless's argv is asserted spelled exactly because mutation showed case-mutation survivors ("docker"->"DOCKER", "info"->"INFO", "--format"->"--FORMAT" fail on case-sensitive filesystems) and lowercasing the Go template returns empty output so every rootless daemon reads as rootful — the fail-open the function exists to prevent; its three-valued contract (True/False/None, with nonzero exit, FileNotFoundError, PermissionError and TimeoutExpired all resolving to None) is driven through subprocess directly, on lines diff-cover had reported unexecuted.

Adding launcher._firewall_runner_argv to the mutation selectors on the PR #461 review pass exposed 19 survivors killed only by an element-for-element argv pin ("run"->"XXrunXX", "--cap-add"->"--CAP-ADD", "root"->"ROOT", "-v"->"-V"), each producing a runtime error or a runner that starts without NET_ADMIN and silently installs no rules — the shape of #429, where the defect hid behind a container that appeared to run fine.

The suite's source sweeps are guarded against passing vacuously the same discipline the mutation layer enforces at mutant granularity: test_userns_mapping's no-bare-keep-id sweep is paired with an AST-bound check that launcher.py and volumes.py still call paths.userns_args, added on PR #461 review after the assertion kept passing while every executable reference was gone, matched only by docstrings.

The targets list contains both ctrquery._runtime and capability._runtime because #456 moved runtime detection down into paths.active_runtime, leaving two thin wrappers — the CLI-facing one printing "neither podman nor docker found on PATH" and exiting 1, the capability-oracle one raising RuntimeError — whose error paths still needed constraining; capability.x__runtime entered the selectors on the PR #461 review pass.
